name: Question 22
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035241/assets/8197d1111bbd4c3b8908bc12cbc58561ffd23fe06d9f9fa99f9ab815ed78733f.png)

The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $y=-\frac{1}{2}.$ Which of the following generates the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{1}{2}.$ 

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2\pi }{3}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035241/assets/ba34bf96662682ec433c3ade0bf3f118638212101a0729fe95bbae05aee8bf1e.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x=\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{4\pi }{3}+2n\pi .
$$

Question 22
?

The graph shows a portion of the curve y=cos⁡x and y=−12. Which of the following generates the x-values of all of their points of intersection? Assume that n is an integer.

a
x=π3+2nπ,x=5π3+2nπ
b
x=5π6+2nπ,x=7π6+2nπ
c
x=2π3+2nπ,x=4π3+2nπ
d
x=π6+2nπ,x=11π6+2nπ
e
x=2π3+2nπ,x=5π3+2nπ
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

At the intersection points, the y-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation cos⁡x=−12.

First, we find the principal value: x1=arccos⁡(−12)=2π3

Our first solution lies in the 2nd quadrant and has a reference angle of θR=π3. Since cos⁡x<0, the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has θR=π3.

Since the second solution x2 lies in the 3rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

x2=π+θR=π+π3=4π3

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is x=2π3+2nπ,x=4π3+2nπ.
